key_insight: DAWG combines belief-propagation ensembles with weighted graph sparsification to maintain competitive quantum error-correction decoding performance while reducing post-processing demand.
engineering_relevance: Less frequent post-processing on a smaller decoding graph could reduce latency tails and specialized hardware resource requirements.
method: Run serial minimum-sum belief propagation on the full detector error model Tanner graph.
Transfer posterior information to a sparsified graph using ensemble-specific transfer matrices, then continue decoding.
Randomize ensemble schedules and apply order-0 Localized Statistics Decoding (LSD-0) as a post-processor.
evidence_signal: Numerical studies on bivariate bicycle codes and superdense color code circuits report DAWG+LSD-0 performance similar to Relay BP and Vibe, with roughly tenfold fewer post-processor calls than Vibe at the same ensemble size.
watch_item: Real-time latency and hardware resource savings remain to be demonstrated beyond the reported numerical evaluations.
paper_title: Decoding with alternating weighted graph sparsification for quantum low-density parity-check codes
